YB-1 can form mRNP-like complexes on RNA in vitro, and these complexes are dynamic structures that can be formed at various YB ratios.
the structural organization of mRNA complexes is determined by YB-1 concentration and that at a high YB1 concentration, this protein is capable of forming a large multimeric complex with mRNA.
the protein YB- 1 is able to form mRNAs with a protein-to-RNA ratio typical for natural mRNP complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of mRNA-YB- 1 complexes at different YB-1 concentrations and with the role of YB-1 in mRNP formation.
the first structural description of mRNA complexes with the universal mRNP protein.
the structural organization of mRNA complexes in which YB-1 serves as a major protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of YB-1 mRNA complexes is determined by the ratio of YB- mRNA and YB-1 protein.
YB-1 can be considered a major protein of mRNPs, but it does not form a stable mRNP scaffold.
in compact YB-1 mRNP complexes, YB- 1 binds to mRNA with its N-terminal RNA-binding domain and forms multimeric Y-shaped complexes with the C-terminal RNA-binding domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of YB-1 mRNA complexes changes depending on the YB-1 concentration, which may be a mechanism of YB- 1-dependent mRNA translation regulation.
YB-1 can form a variety of mRNA complexes, and the type of the complexes formed depends on the YB-1-to-mRNA ratio.
YB-1 can bind mRNA as a monomeric and multimeric protein, and these two forms of YB-1 are functionally distinct.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein composition of mRNP complexes can change dramatically without changing the overall structure of the complex.
YB-1 can be a universal protein of mRNPs, but the protein's function is determined by its ratio on the mRNA molecule and by the structure of the mRNA-bound YB1 complex.
YB-1 can form mRNP structures that are very different from each other in terms of the number of YB-1 molecules per mRNA molecule and the structure of YB- 1 multimers.
